ILOSTAT R package

The ILO’s main online database, ILOSTAT, maintained by the Department of Statistics, is the world’s largest repository of labour market statistics. It covers all countries and regions and a wide range of labour-related topics, including employment, unemployment, wages, working time and labour productivity, to name a few. It includes time series going back as far as 1938; annual, quarterly and monthly labour statistics; country-level, regional and global estimates; and even projections of the main labour market indicators.

ILOSTAT’s website provides immediate access to all its data and related metadata through different ways. Basic users can simply view the desired data online or download it in Excel or csv formats. More advanced users can take advantage of ILOSTAT’s well-structured bulk download facility.

The ilostat R package ('Rilostat') was designed to give data users the ability to access the ILOSTAT database, search for data, rearrange the information as needed, download it in the desired format, and make various data visualizations, all in a programmatic and replicable manner, with the possibility of quickly re-running the queries as required.

Main features of the ILOSTAT R package

  • Provides access to all annual, quarterly, and monthly data available via the ILOSTAT bulk download facility
  • Allows to search for and download data and related metadata in English, French and Spanish
  • Gives the ability to return POSIXct dates for easy integration into plotting and time-series analysis techniques
  • Returns data in long format for direct integration with packages like ggplot2 and dplyr
  • Gives immediate access to the most recent updates
  • Allows for grep-style searching for data descriptions and names

Download and install R from CRAN, install Positron’s IDE, a powerful user interface for R and Python. Then use command:

install.packages("Rilostat")

To install the development version, use the following command:

devtools::install_github("ilostat/Rilostat")

We do not expect to update the ilostat R package too often, but based on questions and remarks from ILOSTAT data users, we will progressively create more examples, tutorials, demos and apps. We will publicly share all of this via Rilostat webpage

SDMX support

Rilostat provides an SDMX-oriented interface through get_ilostat_sdmx(). It reuses the existing Rilostat download, cache and filtering infrastructure while exposing ILOSTAT datasets using SDMX component names and metadata.

The interface supports:

  • observation data as R data frames;
  • data structures;
  • canonical codelists;
  • ILOSTAT dataflows;
  • SDMX-ML 3.1 for structural resources;
  • SDMX-JSON 2.1 for structural resources;
  • English, French and Spanish labels;
  • code, label, short-label and combined code/label representations;
  • SDMX-oriented filtering, including time-period ranges.

Observation data

Observation data can be retrieved using SDMX component identifiers:

x <- get_ilostat_sdmx(
  "UNE_TUNE_SEX_AGE_NB_A",
  filters = list(
    REF_AREA = "FRA",
    SEX = "SEX_F",
    AGE = "AGE_YTHADULT_YGE15"
  )
)

The returned data use SDMX component names such as REF_AREA, SOURCE, FREQ, MEASURE, SEX, AGE, TIME_PERIOD, OBS_VALUE, OBS_STATUS, UNIT_MEASURE and UNIT_MULT.

The SDMX data envelope also identifies the dataflow through STRUCTURE, STRUCTURE_ID and ACTION.

Codes and labels

Codes and labels can be returned together:

x <- get_ilostat_sdmx(
  "UNE_TUNE_SEX_AGE_NB_A",
  type = "both",
  filters = list(
    REF_AREA = "FRA",
    SEX = "SEX_F",
    AGE = "AGE_YTHADULT_YGE15"
  )
)

This returns SDMX code columns together with companion label columns such as REF_AREA_LABEL, SOURCE_LABEL, SEX_LABEL and AGE_LABEL.

The available representations are:

  • type = "code" for SDMX codes;
  • type = "label" for full labels;
  • type = "label_short" for short/display labels where available;
  • type = "both" for codes and labels together.

For example, the AGE code AGE_YTHADULT_YGE15 has the full label Age (Youth, adults): 15+ and the short label 15+.

Filtering

Filters use SDMX component names:

x <- get_ilostat_sdmx(
  "UNE_TUNE_SEX_AGE_NB_A",
  filters = list(
    REF_AREA = "FRA",
    SEX = "SEX_F"
  )
)

Time-period ranges can use comparison operators:

x <- get_ilostat_sdmx(
  "UNE_TUNE_SEX_AGE_NB_A",
  filters = list(
    REF_AREA = "FRA",
    TIME_PERIOD = list(
      ge = "2020",
      le = "2023"
    )
  )
)

FREQ and MEASURE can also be used as filters. They are dataset-level SDMX components; a value incompatible with the selected dataset returns an empty SDMX result.

Data structure

The SDMX-oriented structure of a dataset can be inspected directly:

structure <- get_ilostat_sdmx(
  "UNE_TUNE_SEX_AGE_NB_A",
  resource = "structure"
)

The structure describes the dimensions, time dimension, measure and attributes of the dataset, including their position, representation and associated codelists.

Codelists

Canonical ILOSTAT codelists can be retrieved for coded SDMX components:

age <- get_ilostat_sdmx(
  "UNE_TUNE_SEX_AGE_NB_A",
  resource = "codelist",
  component = "AGE"
)

Other examples include REF_AREA, SOURCE, SEX, OBS_STATUS, UNIT_MEASURE and UNIT_MULT.

Dataflows

Retrieve the dataflow associated with one ILOSTAT dataset:

flow <- get_ilostat_sdmx(
  "UNE_TUNE_SEX_AGE_NB_A",
  resource = "dataflow"
)

The complete ILOSTAT dataflow catalogue can also be retrieved:

flows <- get_ilostat_sdmx(
  resource = "dataflow"
)

SDMX-ML 3.1

Structural resources can be serialized as SDMX-ML 3.1.

For example:

xml <- get_ilostat_sdmx(
  "UNE_TUNE_SEX_AGE_NB_A",
  resource = "structure",
  format = "sdmx-ml"
)

SDMX-ML 3.1 output is available for:

  • resource = "structure";
  • resource = "codelist";
  • resource = "dataflow".

For example, a codelist can be serialized directly:

xml <- get_ilostat_sdmx(
  "UNE_TUNE_SEX_AGE_NB_A",
  resource = "codelist",
  component = "AGE",
  format = "sdmx-ml"
)

SDMX-JSON 2.1

The same structural resources can be serialized as SDMX-JSON 2.1:

json <- get_ilostat_sdmx(
  "UNE_TUNE_SEX_AGE_NB_A",
  resource = "structure",
  format = "sdmx-json"
)

SDMX-JSON 2.1 output is available for structures, codelists and dataflows.

For example:

json <- get_ilostat_sdmx(
  "UNE_TUNE_SEX_AGE_NB_A",
  resource = "codelist",
  component = "AGE",
  format = "sdmx-json"
)

The R data-frame interface, SDMX-ML 3.1 output and SDMX-JSON 2.1 output are generated from the same dataset metadata and SDMX semantic model.

See ?get_ilostat_sdmx for the complete interface.
